papers.title: Functional-Taxonomic Scaling Resolves Conflicting Average Genome Size Estimates Across Environmental Gradients.
papers.abstract: Community-level average genome size (AGS) is a key trait linking microbial diversity, functional potential, and eco-evolutionary strategy, yet estimates of AGS diverge markedly among common methods. Here, we introduce and validate a framework that adjudicates conflicting AGS estimates by testing which estimate yields a gap between scaled functional diversity and scaled taxonomic diversity that is consistent with the expected positive association between genome size and gene functional breadth. Across independent environmental gradients, metagenomic AGS estimates align with this framework and e
papers.summary: The authors introduce a framework to resolve conflicting estimates of average genome size (AGS) in microbial communities by testing which method produces a functional-taxonomic diversity gap consistent with the expected link between genome size and gene functional breadth. Across independent environmental gradients, metagenomic AGS estimates align with this framework, helping adjudicate between divergent methods.

papers.title: Microbial filtering and functional reprogramming in soil exposed to spent NCM battery black powder.
papers.abstract: Spent lithium-ion battery black powder is an emerging complex contaminant, which contains transition metals, residual electrolyte salts, and compounds derived from organic electrolytes or binders. Its ecological effects on soil microbiomes remain poorly understood. Here, we designed a soil microcosm experiment with using red soil exposed to a concentration gradient of black powder derived from nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) lithium-ion batteries. Samples were collected at two incubation time points and analyzed by shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Black powder exposure produced a nonlinear taxono
papers.summary: This study used soil microcosm experiments and shotgun metagenomics to examine how spent NCM lithium-ion battery black powder affects soil microbial communities. Exposure caused non-linear taxonomic shifts, with microbial filtering and functional reprogramming of the soil microbiome. The work highlights ecological risks of battery waste contamination in soils.

papers.title: Clinical severity score-guided metagenomic analysis identifying gut microbial taxonomic and functional markers for severe hepatitis E progression.
papers.abstract: Although gut microbiome alterations have been reported in hepatitis E (HE), the taxonomic and functional determinants of disease severity remain poorly defined. Here, we performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 125 individuals spanning acute non-icteric hepatitis (ANIH), acute icteric hepatitis (AIH), acute liver failure (ALF), and healthy controls. We constructed a surrogate clinical severity index from routine blood parameters and developed an integrative analytical framework that combined XGBoost-based taxonomic modeling with LASSO-driven functional feature selection t
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of fecal samples from 125 individuals across a spectrum of hepatitis E severity (from non-icteric to acute liver failure) to identify gut microbial taxonomic and functional markers associated with disease progression. By building a clinical severity index from routine blood parameters and combining XGBoost-based taxonomic modeling with LASSO-driven functional feature selection, the authors pinpoint microbial signatures that track with severe hepatitis E. The work suggests that gut microbiome features could serve as non-invasive markers for stratifying hepatitis E patients.

papers.title: Long-Read Metagenomic Characterization of the Microbial DNA and Resistome Recovered from a Peracetic Acid Immersion Chiller in a Commercial Poultry Processing Facility: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Peracetic acid (PAA)-based immersion chillers are a critical pathogen intervention in commercial poultry processing, yet the microbial DNA recoverable from these systems remains poorly characterized. Here, we applied long-read Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT) metagenomics to characterize the taxonomic composition, resistance gene content, and mobile element context of the microbial DNA recovered from the mid-stage immersion chiller of a commercial poultry processing facility. From 14.47 GB of sequencing data (median Q-score 19.1), we reconstructed three near-complete metagenome-assembled genom
papers.summary: This pilot study used long-read Oxford Nanopore metagenomics to characterize the microbial DNA and resistance genes (resistome) present in a peracetic acid immersion chiller at a commercial poultry processing facility. From 14.47 GB of sequencing data, the authors reconstructed three near-complete metagenome-assembled genomes, providing a first look at the taxonomic composition and mobile genetic element context of antimicrobial resistance in this critical pathogen intervention system.

papers.title: MOSHPIT: Accessible, reproducible metagenome data science on the QIIME 2 framework.
papers.abstract: Metagenome sequencing has revolutionized functional microbiome analysis across diverse ecosystems but is fraught with technical hurdles. We introduce MOSHPIT (MOdular SHotgun metagenome Pipelines with Integrated provenance Tracking; https://moshpit.qiime2.org)-software built on the QIIME 2/rachis framework (Q2F) that integrates best-in-class CAMI II- and LEMMI-validated metagenome tools with robust provenance tracking and multiple user interfaces-enabling streamlined, reproducible metagenome analysis for all expertise levels. By building on Q2F, MOSHPIT enhances scalability, interoperability,
papers.summary: MOSHPIT is a new software package built on the QIIME 2 framework that integrates validated shotgun metagenome analysis tools with built-in provenance tracking and multiple user interfaces. It aims to make reproducible metagenome data science accessible to researchers at all expertise levels, from beginners to advanced bioinformaticians.

papers.title: Coincidental observation of a parvovirus during a targeted bacterial survey of cattle suffering from septic arthritis.
papers.abstract: DNA capture-based sequencing by hybridization probe enrichment (CapSeq) affords high-throughput and targeted gene-to-organism detection. Despite the specificity designed into CapSeq platforms, untargeted DNA represent additional genes and organisms of interest. To this end, de novo metagenome assemblies of CapSeq datasets present opportunities for discovery. We report an example here. CapSeq of samples that originated from cattle suffering from septic arthritis resulted in detection and assembly of two ungulate tetraparvovirus 1 (UTPV1) genomes. These coincidental detections and assemblies wer
papers.summary: While using a targeted DNA capture sequencing approach (CapSeq) to survey bacteria in cattle with septic arthritis, the authors unexpectedly assembled two complete genomes of ungulate tetraparvovirus 1 (UTPV1). This demonstrates that off-target reads in targeted enrichment datasets can be repurposed for viral discovery through de novo metagenome assembly.

papers.title: "Quadrupling" the protein family space with global metagenomics.
papers.abstract: The known universe of protein families represents only a small fraction of nature's molecular diversity. From 40.3 billion predicted open reading frames across 40 446 metagenomes, 9540 metatranscriptomes, and 539 million proteins from 167 415 reference genomes, we identified 608 258 previously uncharacterized putative protein families with ≥100 members and 6.5 million families with ≥25 members, none matching known Pfam domains or reference proteins. This effort doubles the known repertoire of large families and quadruples that of smaller families. Integration of AlphaFold2-based structural pre
papers.summary: By mining over 40 billion predicted open reading frames from tens of thousands of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes, the authors identified 608,258 previously uncharacterized protein families with at least 100 members, plus 6.5 million smaller families, none matching known Pfam domains or reference proteins. This roughly doubles the known repertoire of large protein families and quadruples that of smaller families, substantially expanding the known protein family space. AlphaFold2-based structural predictions were integrated to help characterize these novel families.

papers.title: Prescribed burns drive lasting changes in soil nitrogen cycling and microbial function.
papers.abstract: Fire is a major pulse disturbance to soil microbial communities, with broad implications for nutrient cycling; however, regular burning is also a natural and often-essential process maintaining biodiversity in unique and imperiled fire-dependent ecosystems. Prescribed fire is widely used to promote this biodiversity and simultaneously reduce wildfire risk. Although such repeated burning is known to alter surface biodiversity, belowground soil geochemistry, and soil microbial community structure, the functional consequences (i.e., the metabolic capabilities that underlie the ecosystem services
papers.summary: This study shows that repeated prescribed burns cause lasting shifts in soil nitrogen cycling and the functional capabilities of soil microbial communities. The findings suggest that while prescribed fire supports aboveground biodiversity and reduces wildfire risk, it also has persistent belowground consequences for nutrient cycling and microbial ecosystem services.

papers.title: Dental spittoon biofilms as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance: a longitudinal multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Dental chair spittoons are chronically exposed to saliva, aerosols, intermittent water flow, and chemical disinfectants, yet their biofilm ecology and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dynamics remain poorly defined. We applied longitudinal 16S rRNA gene sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and culture-based antimicrobial susceptibility testing to biofilms collected across four dental departments at three time points. Community analyses revealed significant temporal succession and department-specific structuring, indicating the establishment of stable, ecologically differentiated biofilm systems. Nu
papers.summary: This longitudinal multi-omics study characterized biofilms in dental chair spittoons across four departments and three time points, revealing stable, department-specific microbial communities that undergo temporal succession. The biofilms harbor diverse antimicrobial resistance genes and resistant isolates, suggesting spittoons act as persistent reservoirs for AMR in dental settings.

papers.title: Viral Metagenomic Sequencing Reveals Viral Codetection Patterns in Children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections, yet the frequency and composition of viral codetections in affected children have not been extensively profiled using unbiased sequencing approaches. Here, we performed viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs collected from 42 pediatric patients with confirmed RSV infection to characterize the codetection landscape. RSV was detected and genotyped in all specimens. Beyond RSV, we identified nine additional human respiratory viruses coexisting across the cohort; several of these fall outside th
papers.summary: This study used unbiased viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs from 42 children with confirmed RSV infection to profile which other viruses co-occur. RSV was detected and genotyped in all samples, and nine additional human respiratory viruses were found across the cohort, including some not typically covered by standard diagnostic panels. The work highlights how metagenomic approaches can reveal a broader viral codetection landscape than targeted testing.

papers.title: Multidimensional Physiological and Gut Microbiome Profiling Identifies Subtle Physiological Patterns in an Apparently Healthy Aging Indian Cohort: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Aging is characterized by gradual shifts in cellular and physiological processes, even in individuals who remain apparently clinically healthy. These changes reflect a coordinated decline in metabolic efficiency, immune regulation, organ function, psychological resilience, and sleep integrity, domains increasingly recognized as interconnected determinants of apparently healthy aging. This study explored age- and sex-associated patterns in multidimensional physiological domains and gut microbiota features among 45 apparently healthy middle-aged and elderly participants across four age-sex group
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study profiled 45 apparently healthy middle-aged and elderly Indian adults across multiple physiological domains and gut microbiome features, finding subtle age- and sex-associated patterns even in clinically healthy individuals. The work highlights that physiological and microbial shifts during aging can be detected before overt disease, though the small sample limits generalizability.

papers.title: Validating a high-throughput in vitro model for culturing antibiotic-altered microbiome communities.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome plays a central role in host health, and its disruption is associated with metabolic, infectious, and immune conditions. Stool sampling is frequently used to characterize snapshots of the gut microbiota. To screen microbiota communities in vitro, multi-stage bioreactors have been developed that model distinct physiological environments along the gastrointestinal tract. However, such bioreactors are often operationally complex and provide limited throughput. Stool-derived in vitro communities offer several advantages to study microbiota due to their ease of use, high-throughp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint validates a high-throughput in vitro system for culturing stool-derived microbial communities that have been altered by antibiotics. The approach aims to make microbiome screening simpler and more scalable than multi-stage bioreactors while still capturing community responses to antibiotic perturbation. It provides a practical platform for testing how drugs affect gut microbial communities outside the host.

papers.title: Longitudinal Stability of the Gut Microbiota in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Prospective Observational Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a key role in immune regulation in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet longitudinal data on microbiome dynamics and their relationships with disability and biomarkers remain limited. This study aimed to identify longitudinal gut microbiome changes in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) and their association with disability and specific serum biomarkers, including predicted metabolic pathways. In this prospective longitudinal study, 29 treatment-naïve RRMS patients were evaluated at baseline and after one year of disease-modifying therapy. Clinical asse
papers.summary: This prospective study tracked gut microbiome composition in 29 treatment-naive relapsing-remitting MS patients over one year of disease-modifying therapy, examining links to disability and serum biomarkers. The work provides longitudinal evidence on microbiome stability and dynamics in MS, though the small cohort limits generalizability.

papers.title: Gut, Oral, and Fungal Microbiota in Hypertension: A Multi-Compartment Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota is an established modulator of blood pressure, but the oral bacteriome and the fungal mycobiome have been examined largely in isolation from it and from each other. No previous synthesis has evaluated all three compartments within one analytical framework, or treated sex and ethnicity as primary analytical axes rather than adjustment covariates. Systematic review reported according to PRISMA 2020 and, for the synthesis, the SWiM guideline. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 30 June 2026. Observational human studies in adults re
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes human observational studies examining the gut bacteriome, oral bacteriome, and fungal mycobiome together in relation to hypertension, a multi-compartment approach not previously attempted. It also treats sex and ethnicity as primary analytical axes rather than adjustment covariates, aiming to clarify how these host factors shape microbiota-hypertension associations.

papers.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing and Intestinal Metagenome Sequencing Revealed the Carriage and Transmission of Salmonella enterica in Xinjiang, China.
papers.abstract: Background:Salmonella enterica, a major foodborne pathogen, poses a severe global public health threat. However, data regarding its carriage characteristics, transmission patterns, and association with intestinal microbiota in healthy populations of Xinjiang, China, remain insufficient, limiting the formulation of targeted salmonellosis prevention and control strategies. Methods: In this study, 31 Salmonella enterica strains isolated from more than 2000 healthy individuals in Urumqi were subjected to whole-genome sequencing to analyze serovars, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, and virulen
papers.summary: This study used whole-genome sequencing of 31 Salmonella enterica strains from over 2,000 healthy individuals in Urumqi, Xinjiang, to characterize serovars, antimicrobial resistance genes, and virulence factors. Intestinal metagenome sequencing was also performed to examine how Salmonella carriage relates to gut microbiota composition and potential transmission patterns. The findings aim to inform targeted prevention and control strategies for salmonellosis in this understudied region.

papers.title: Sexual Propagation Enhances Tea Quality Through Rhizosphere Microbiome Assembly and Metabolic Reprogramming in Camellia sinensis.
papers.abstract: Tea quality is largely determined by the accumulation of specialized metabolites in fresh leaves, yet the effects of the propagation method on tea quality and its belowground ecological basis remain insufficiently understood. In this study, sexually propagated (SR) and asexually propagated (AR) tea plants were compared by integrating soil physicochemical analysis, leaf quality and physiological measurements, widely targeted metabolomics, and rhizosphere metagenomic profiling. Compared with AR, SR plants exhibited more favorable rhizosphere nutrient conditions, with soil organic matter, total n
papers.summary: This study compared sexually propagated (seed-grown) and asexually propagated (clonal) tea plants, integrating soil chemistry, leaf metabolomics, and rhizosphere metagenomics. Sexually propagated plants showed improved rhizosphere nutrient conditions, distinct rhizosphere microbiome assembly, and metabolic reprogramming in leaves associated with better tea quality. The findings suggest that propagation method shapes belowground microbial communities that influence aboveground specialized metabolite accumulation.

papers.title: Structural and Functional Characterisation of a Metagenome-Derived CYP108D18 Reveals an Unusual Dioxygen-Bound State and Selective Hydrocarbon Hydroxylation.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 enzymes form a large superfamily of monooxygenases capable of oxidising diverse substrates. Among them, members of the CYP108 family are recognised for their role in monoterpenoid oxidation. In this study, we report the identification and characterisation of a new CYP108 family member, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome derived from microbial communities in a geothermal hot spring located in northern Queensland, Australia. Taxonomic binning associated CYP108D18 with a Novosphingobium species, a genus well-known for its bioremediation potential. CYP108D18 was heterolo
papers.summary: Researchers identified and characterized a new cytochrome P450 enzyme, CYP108D18, from a metagenome-assembled genome of a geothermal hot spring microbial community, linking it to a Novosphingobium species. The enzyme displays an unusual dioxygen-bound state and selectively hydroxylates hydrocarbons, expanding knowledge of CYP108 family function beyond monoterpenoid oxidation.

papers.title: From Rhizosphere to Resistance: Microbe-Plant Interactions in Eco-Smart Biocontrol.
papers.abstract: The increasing limitations of chemical pesticides such as environmental pollution, pathogen resistance, and threats to human and ecosystem health have increased the demand for sustainable, biologically based crop protection methods. Eco-smart biocontrol has emerged as a game-changing paradigm that uses beneficial microorganisms associated with plants to suppress phytopathogens, boost plant immunity, and make agroecosystems more resilient over time. Moving beyond traditional single-strain biocontrol, eco-smart biocontrol integrates multi-omics discovery, artificial intelligence-assisted predict
papers.summary: This review examines how beneficial microorganisms in the plant rhizosphere can be harnessed for sustainable crop protection, replacing chemical pesticides. It highlights an 'eco-smart biocontrol' paradigm that combines multi-omics discovery with AI-assisted prediction to design more resilient biocontrol strategies beyond traditional single-strain approaches.

papers.title: Comparing the Performance of Double-Stranded and Single-Stranded DNA Libraries for Ancient Oral Microbiome Reconstruction.
papers.abstract: DNA library construction methods can affect the recovery of ancient DNA, thus influencing downstream analyses. While single-stranded library preparation (ssLib) has been shown to outperform double-stranded (dsLib) for highly degraded vertebrate host DNA, especially for samples older than 40,000 years, few studies have examined how library protocols shape ancient microbial community reconstruction. Here, we compare the sequencing output of paired ssLib and dsLib dental calculus libraries generated from 12 Neanderthals and two Chalcolithic humans, prepared using implementations of the Gansauge e
papers.summary: This study compares single-stranded (ssLib) and double-stranded (dsLib) DNA library preparation methods for reconstructing ancient oral microbiomes from dental calculus of 12 Neanderthals and two Chalcolithic humans. While ssLib is known to improve recovery of highly degraded host DNA, this work examines whether it also benefits ancient microbial community reconstruction, finding differences in sequencing output that could affect downstream microbiome analyses.

papers.title: Phylogeny-guided curation reveals widespread misannotation of Asgard archaeal 16S rRNA gene sequences in public databases.
papers.abstract: Accurate taxonomic assignment of 16S rRNA gene sequences is essential for the reliable interpretation of microbial community studies based on amplicon sequence data. Yet, it critically depends on the reliability of reference databases such as the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB) and the SILVA ribosomal RNA database. Here, we evaluate the consistency of taxonomic annotations within the Asgardarchaeota phylum, a lineage of major evolutionary and ecological interest. Using a phylogenetically curated set of GTDB-derived 16S rRNA gene sequences, we show that most of the affiliations of these sequenc
papers.summary: The authors used a phylogenetically curated set of Asgard archaeal 16S rRNA sequences to test whether public reference databases (GTDB and SILVA) assign these sequences to the correct taxonomy. They found that most affiliations of these sequences are misannotated, revealing widespread errors in taxonomic assignment for this evolutionarily important lineage. This has direct implications for the reliability of microbial community studies that depend on these databases.

papers.title: Stage-specific cyanobacterial handoffs and heterotrophic subsidies underpin biocrust carbon accumulation.
papers.abstract: Inoculating cyanobacteria is a widely adopted strategy to accelerate biocrust formation and restore dryland soil functions, yet the in situ mechanisms sustaining microbial biomass carbon (MBC) accumulation under seasonal stress remain poorly understood. Here, we combined a field inoculation experiment with multi-omic profiling (amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metaproteomics) and genome-scale metabolic modeling to track the circannual development of induced cyanobacterial biocrusts in Hopq Desert, China. Although the inoculated Konicacronema strain (formerly Microcol
papers.summary: This study tracked the year-round development of cyanobacteria-inoculated biocrusts in a Chinese desert using multi-omics and metabolic modeling, revealing that different cyanobacterial taxa dominate at different seasonal stages and hand off metabolic roles over time. Heterotrophic microbes receive carbon subsidies from cyanobacteria, and this staged cooperation drives microbial biomass carbon accumulation under seasonal stress.

papers.title: Personalized whole-body modeling links gut microbiota to metabolic perturbations in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome has been linked to metabolic disturbances in Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the mechanisms by which gut microbes might influence metabolic dysfunction in AD remain poorly understood. Previously, gut microbiome-personalized whole-body models of human metabolism have been applied to predict how altered gut microbiome compositions may influence metabolites in the blood of healthy aging individuals with increased risk of AD. However, these previous results have not been validated in AD. In this study, we aimed to test these prior predictions in a cohort of AD dementia
papers.summary: This study uses personalized whole-body metabolic models to test whether gut microbiome composition can predict metabolic perturbations in Alzheimer's disease patients. The authors validate prior predictions from healthy aging models against a cohort of AD dementia patients, linking specific gut microbes to metabolic changes in the blood. The work supports a mechanistic connection between the gut microbiome and AD-associated metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Dataset characterising dominant bacterial phylotypes across animal manure-enriched composting microcosms for crude oil waste sludge bioremediation.
papers.abstract: The dataset provides a complete record of microbial, functional, physicochemical, and contaminant dynamics from controlled co-composting microcosms designed to remediate petroleum refinery sludge using targeted animal manure amendments. Five treatments-cow, pig, horse, and poultry manures, as well as an unamended control-were monitored over 300 days. The study incorporated amplicon-based 16S rRNA gene sequencing, functional gene inference, culture-based validation, bulk chemistry, and chromatographic analyses. Illumina MiSeq profiling of the V1-V3 regions identified 359 bacterial genera (raw O
papers.summary: This dataset tracks microbial community dynamics, functional gene profiles, physicochemical properties, and contaminant degradation across five manure-amended composting microcosms (cow, pig, horse, poultry, and unamended control) used to bioremediate petroleum refinery sludge over 300 days. It combines 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, functional gene inference, culture-based validation, and chromatographic chemistry to identify dominant bacterial phylotypes driving remediation. The resource is intended to support reuse and comparative analyses of manure-driven bioremediation strategies.

papers.title: Functional organization outweighs spatial separation in structuring microbial communities across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume.
papers.abstract: Petroleum-hydrocarbon plumes in groundwater are shaped by hydrological transport, redox conditions, and indigenous microbial activity. However, it remains unclear whether spatial differences among groundwater microbiomes primarily reflect physical separation among wells or ecological reorganization associated with distinct attenuation states within a plume.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether microbial community differences across a petroleum-hydrocarbon groundwater plume are driven mainly by physical distance between sampling wells or by ecological reorganization tied to different contaminant attenuation states. The authors find that functional organization of the communities, rather than spatial separation, is the dominant structuring factor. This suggests that plume biogeochemistry, not geography, primarily shapes microbiome composition and function.

papers.title: Microbial niches at the One Health interface: linking environmental factors, biomes, and disease dynamics.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities shape life at every stratum of environmental hierarchy, ranging from a wide spectrum of functionalities such as nutrient cycling processes that support ecosystem functioning in soil biome to those of intricate balance between disease causal and responsive immune defenses in animals. This review explores the roles of microbial niches in shaping pathogen persistence, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dissemination, and host-microbe interactions at the human-animal-environment interface. Emphasis is placed on microbial community assembly, environmental drivers of pathogen survi
papers.summary: This review examines how microbial communities at the human-animal-environment interface influence pathogen persistence, antimicrobial resistance spread, and host-microbe interactions. It emphasizes the ecological and environmental drivers that shape microbial community assembly and disease dynamics within a One Health framework.

papers.title: Combined abdominal and transcranial photobiomodulation is associated with fecal microbiome restructuring: a systems microbiology pre-post case report.
papers.abstract: Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been proposed as a non-invasive strategy capable of modulating mitochondrial, inflammatory, vascular, and gut-brain axis-related pathways. However, its potential effects on fecal microbiome ecology in neurobehavioral conditions remain poorly characterized. This case report describes paired fecal microbiome findings before and after a 90-day combined abdominal and transcranial PBM protocol in a 6-year-old female with autism spectrum disorder and chronic constipation. PBM was delivered daily using a 1064-nm near-infrared LED device with 54 mW/cm2 irradiance, applied
papers.summary: This case report describes fecal microbiome changes in a 6-year-old girl with autism spectrum disorder and chronic constipation who underwent a 90-day combined abdominal and transcranial photobiomodulation (near-infrared LED) protocol. Paired before-and-after stool samples suggest the intervention may be associated with restructuring of the gut microbiome, though the single-case design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Bronchoalveolar Lavage Microbiota in Critically Ill Patients with Aspiration Pneumonia: An Exploratory Comparison with Community-Acquired Pneumonia and Analysis of Gemella Detection and Mortality.
papers.abstract: Aspiration pneumonia (AP) is a common and severe infection among critically ill older adults, but its lower respiratory tract microbiota and clinical associations remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory study characterizes the bronchoalveolar lavage microbiota in critically ill patients with aspiration pneumonia and compares it to community-acquired pneumonia, with a specific focus on Gemella detection and its relationship to mortality. The findings suggest distinct microbial signatures in aspiration pneumonia that may have prognostic implications.

papers.title: Gut microbiome-metabolome signatures of osteosarcopenia in fracture patients in China.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcopenia, defined as the coexistence of low bone mass and sarcopenia, is a disabling musculoskeletal condition, yet its gut microbial and metabolic characteristics in clinical populations remain incompletely understood. Integrative multi-omics approaches may help clarify species-metabolite networks associated with this condition, particularly in fracture patients.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated multi-omics to characterize gut microbiome and metabolome signatures in Chinese fracture patients with osteosarcopenia, a condition combining low bone mass and muscle loss. It aims to identify species-metabolite networks associated with the disease, addressing a gap in clinical understanding of the gut-muscle-bone axis.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of the fecal microbiome in Lamp2 knockout mice reveals limited genotype-associated differences under standard housing.
papers.abstract: Lysosomal pathways influence host-microbe interactions, but the microbiome consequences of lysosomal dysfunction remain incompletely defined. LAMP2 is required for autophagosome-lysosome fusion, and pathogenic variants in LAMP2 cause Danon disease. Whether Lamp2 loss alters the gut microbiome in vivo has not been systematically evaluated using methods that profile both taxonomic composition and microbial functional potential, such as shotgun metagenomics.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the fecal microbiome of Lamp2 knockout mice, which model Danon disease, compared to wild-type mice under standard housing conditions. Despite the known role of LAMP2 in autophagy and host-microbe interactions, the analysis found only limited taxonomic and functional differences associated with the genotype. The results suggest that Lamp2 loss alone does not substantially reshape the gut microbiome in this controlled setting.

papers.title: Genome-resolved gut metagenomics identifies an Escherichia coli-Collinsella signature associated with Wagner 4 gangrenous diabetic foot ulcers.
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are a major complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus, but whether the gut microbiome captures systemic microbial features associated with advanced ulcer severity remains unclear. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 43 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and active DFU, comparing Wagner grades 1-3 (n = 30) with Wagner 4 gangrenous disease (n = 13). De novo assembly and binning recovered 440 dereplicated metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) meeting medium-quality or high-completeness/low-contamination thresholds. Community-level diversit
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 43 type 2 diabetes patients with active diabetic foot ulcers to compare gut microbiome features between Wagner grades 1-3 and Wagner grade 4 gangrenous disease. De novo assembly and binning recovered 440 metagenome-assembled genomes, revealing an Escherichia coli-Collinsella signature associated with the more severe gangrenous ulcers. The findings suggest that gut microbiome composition may reflect or contribute to systemic features linked to DFU severity.
